  5|법왕 굉도의 죽음. 그리고 무림의 태산북두인 소림사에서 벌어진 의문의 혈겁(血劫).
  6|
  7|달리는 말보다 빠른 것이 사람들의 목소리다.
  8|
  9|수많은 목격자들의 입을 통해 소문은 일파만파 퍼졌다.
 10|
 11|“다들 그 소식 들었나? 성라대연에서…….”
 12|
 13|“무림인들이 숭산을 에워싸고 있네. 소림사에서 혈겁이 벌어졌다더군.”
 14|
 15|성라대연을 맞이하여 축제 분위기에 들떠 있던 하남성은 발칵 뒤집혔다.
 16|
 17|노인은 수십여 년 전 천하를 휩쓸었던 마교의 준동을 떠올렸고, 젊은이는 케케묵은 과거라 취급했던 전쟁이 현실로 다가왔다는 사실을 깨달았다.
 18|
 19|“마교가 나타나다니, 큰일이야. 큰일.”
 20|
 21|“일설에 의하면 마교가 아니라 다른 놈들이 저지른 짓이라던데?”
 22|
 23|“그런 짓을 저지를 만한 놈들이 마교 말고도 또 있단 말인가?”
 24|
 25|“정확한 사실까지는 나도 잘 몰라. 그냥 오다가다 들었네.”
 26|
 27|“그럴 리가. 이번에 소림을 습격한 흉수들의 우두머리가 그 무시무시한 음양쌍괴(陰陽雙怪)라던데.”
 28|
 29|“음양쌍괴? 나는 마교주인 천마(天魔)가 직접 나섰다고 들었네만.”
 30|
 31|“처, 천마?”
 32|
 33|여러 가지 말들이 쌓이고 쌓이니 소문은 눈덩이처럼 불어났다.
 34|
 35|사실과 거짓 속에서 혼란을 겪던 사람들의 이목이 한 곳을 향해 쏠린 것은 당연한 일이었다.
 36|
 37|무림맹의 옛터.
 38|
 39|정파 무림의 크고 작은 기둥들이 위치한 그곳으로.
 40|
 41|
 42|
 43|* * *
 44|
 45|
 46|
 47|“이야기 들었습니다. 종리추, 아니 검성 매종학 대협에 관해서요.”
 48|
 49|“…….”
 50|
 51|“힘내십쇼. 살다 보면 그럴 수도 있죠.”
 52|
 53|“…….”
 54|
 55|“저도 이번에 완전히 알거지, 휴우……. 여하간 그렇게 됐는데. 조장님 소식 듣고 힘이 솟더라고요.”
 56|
 57|“왜?”
 58|
 59|“예?”
 60|
 61|“왜 힘이 솟냐고.”
 62|
 63|“그거야 당연한 이치 아닙니까. 옛 성현들이 말씀하시길, 아픔은 나눌수록 가벼워진다고…….”
 64|
 65|퍽!
 66|
 67|“흐억.”
 68|
 69|정확히 명치를 가격당한 혁무진이 바람 빠지는 소리를 내며 허리를 숙였다.
 70|
 71|훤히 드러난 뒤통수를 보자 저절로 손이 간다. 손이 가.
 72|
 73|빡!
 74|
 75|“힘이 솟구치냐? 어?”
 76|
 77|“자, 잠시만요. 명치 맞았어요. 명치.”
 78|
 79|“저는요. 니 새끼 때문에 혈압이 솟구쳐요. 피가 거꾸로 솟아요!”
 80|
 81|빡빡빡!
 82|
 83|폭풍처럼 뒤통수를 후려치고 나자 속이 좀 풀린다.
 84|
 85|이 자식은 가뜩이나 심란한데 사람을 건드리고 난리야.
 86|
 87|“지금 분위기 심각하니까 말조심해라. 응?”
 88|
 89|혁무진이 뒤통수를 문지르며 중얼거렸다.
 90|
 91|“너무 심각해 보여서 풀어 드리려고 한 건데.”
 92|
 93|“그냥 조용히 있어, 인마.”
 94|
 95|“……옙.”
 96|
 97|혁무진을 침묵시킨 나는 가만히 창밖을 바라봤다.
 98|
 99|정신없이 사방을 오고 가는 무인들과 누구 하나 티 내는 사람이 없는데도 긴장감이 흐르는 분위기.
100|
101|그러나 그 와중에도 하늘은 화창하기 그지없었다.
102|
103|힘 빠진 혁무진의 목소리가 귓가를 파고들었다.
104|
105|“기분이 이상하네요.”
106|
107|“뭐가.”
108|
109|“그냥. 다 실감이 안 나요. 고작 하루밖에 지나지 않았다는 것이.”
110|
111|“나도 그래.”
112|
113|파란만장이라는 말로도 부족하다. 전날 있었던 모든 일이 무엇 하나 실감 나지 않았다. 전부 꿈처럼 느껴질 만큼.
114|
115|마지막 숨을 내쉬던 굉도와 피로 물든 소림사의 광경이 눈앞을 스치고 음양쌍괴와 혈주, 검성 매종학의 등장까지 파노라마처럼 펼쳐졌다.
116|
117|‘문제는 이게 프롤로그라는 거지.’
118|
119|영화관이었다면 슬슬 엔딩 크레딧이 올라와도 이상하지 않은 타이밍. 하지만 이건 불길한 전조에 지나지 않는다.
120|
121|모두가 예감하는 왠지 모를 위기감이 피부로 느껴질 정도였다.
122|
123|‘뭔가가 바뀌고 있다.’
124|
125|작금의 천하는 이미 거대한 화약고로 변해 버렸다. 도화선을 쥔 것은 정파 무림이지만 암천의 손에는 부싯돌이 들려 있었다.
126|
127|그리고 바로 어제, 도화선에 불이 붙었다.
128|
129|이 모든 일의 결말은 아직 모르겠지만 과정은 짐작할 수 있었다.
130|
131|‘전쟁이 일어나겠지.’
132|
133|산서성 때와는 차원이 다른 전쟁이 일어날 것이다.
134|
135|나도 내심 짐작하고 있는 것을 수뇌부가 모를 리 없다.
136|
137|정파 무림의 수뇌부는 이미 이번 사건의 사태 수습과 회의에 여념이 없었다.
138|
139|“참. 그러고 보니까 조장님도 어제 회의 참석하지 않으셨습니까?”
140|
141|나는 작게 고개를 끄덕였다.
142|
143|구파일방이나 오대세가에 비할 바는 아니지만, 태원 진가도 엄연한 산서성의 패자다.
144|
145|특히나 산서성은 암천이 처음 모습을 드러낸 곳이니 수뇌부들의 지대한 관심이 몰린 것은 당연했다.
146|
147|“뭐랍니까?”
148|
149|“대장로와 적풍단에 관해서 묻더라고. 아는 선에서 다 대답해 줬지.”
150|
151|“대장로는 그렇다 치고 적풍단이요?”
152|
153|“적풍단주 풍양이 썼던 잠력단(暫力丹)이 암천과 연관이 있으니까.”
154|
155|“아.”
156|
157|혁무진도 이제는 가문의 고위 관계자라 어느 정도의 사정은 알고 있다. 잠력단과 암천의 존재 역시 마찬가지다.
158|
159|“다른 이야기는 없었습니까?”
160|
161|“그냥 나왔어. 어차피 중요한 소식은 큰형님이 듣고 전해 줄 테고…….”
162|
163|입술 사이로 나도 모르게 가라앉은 목소리가 흘러나왔다.
164|
165|“노야를 계속 혼자 놔두기에는 불안해서.”
166|
167|창밖을 바라보던 시선이 저절로 한 사람을 향했다.
168|
169|깊은 잠에 빠진 것처럼 침상에 누워 있는 자그마한 체구의 노인.
170|
171|주름진 손을 잡자 맥박이 느껴지고 작게나마 오르락내리락하는 움직임에선 호흡이 느껴졌지만, 그는 하루가 지난 지금까지도 정신을 차리지 못했다.
172|
173|“언제쯤 깨어나실까요?”
174|
175|“그걸 정확히 모르는 게 문제지.”
176|
177|“그 누구더라, 명의로 이름이 자자한 의원 하나가 다녀가지 않았습니까?”
178|
179|“자기도 손쓸 방법이 없대. 다른 사람들처럼 크게 다친 것도 아니니까 우선은 지켜보자고 하더라고.”
180|
181|화신귀무(火神鬼武). 열화문의 정수라고 할 수 있는 신공.
182|
183|천 명의 무인을 대적할 수 있을 만큼 엄청난 위력을 지녔지만, 모든 일에는 그만한 대가가 따르는 법이다.
184|
185|이미 백 세를 훌쩍 넘은 노인에게는 그 여파를 감당할 체력과 힘이 남아 있지 않았다.
186|
187|‘어쩌면…….’
188|
189|문득 떠오르는 생각을, 고개를 흔들어 털어 버렸다.
190|
191|부정적인 생각은 접어 두자.
192|
193|검성도, 의원도 분명히 목숨에 지장은 없다고 말했다. 지금은 적천강을 곁에서 지켜보는 것이 최선이었다.
194|
195|“내가 자리 비우는 동안 수상쩍은 놈은 없었지?”
196|
197|무림맹 내부에서 소림사 방장이 암살당했다. 누구도 안전하다 할 수 없었다. 적천강이 혈주로부터 나를 지켰듯이, 나도 그를 지켜야 한다.
198|
199|혁무진이 자신 있다는 듯한 표정으로 고개를 끄덕였다.
200|
201|“진룡대(進龍隊)가 전각을 빈틈없이 에워싸고 있습니다. 걱정하지 마십쇼.”
202|
203|“진룡대? 태원 진가의 최정예라는 거기?”
204|
205|“예. 소가주님께서도 적 대협의 안위를 걱정하셔서 저를 붙이셨습니다. 제가 누굽니까? 진룡대의 부대주, 혁무진 아닙니까?”
206|
207|“어…….”
208|
209|나는 녀석을 위아래로 훑어보다가 슬쩍 시선을 피했다.
210|
211|자신감에 가득 차 있던 혁무진의 표정이 대번에 떨떠름해졌다.
212|
213|“뭡니까, 방금 그 반응은?”
214|
215|“아무것도 아냐. 그냥 앞으로는 내가 자리를 비우면 안 되겠다는 생각이 들어서.”
216|
217|“설마 지금 본가 최정예인 진룡대의 실력을 못 믿으시는 겁니까?”
218|
219|“어허. 아니라니까. 그냥 넘어가.”
220|
221|게슴츠레한 눈으로 나를 노려보던 혁무진이 벌떡 일어났다.
222|
223|“됐습니다. 그냥 소가주님께 보고드리고 철수시키겠습니다.”
224|
225|“에헤이, 말을 왜 또 그렇게 하냐. 요즘 사춘기야?”
226|
227|“조장님이 너무 섭섭하게 말씀하시니까 그런 것 아닙니까. 이게 한두 번이에요? 예?!”
228|
229|“목소리 줄여. 노야 깨신다.”
230|
231|“깨면 좋죠.”
232|
233|“…….”
234|
235|그건 그러네.
236|
237|내가 순간 할 말을 잃은 사이 혁무진이 문을 향해 걸음을 뗐다.
238|
239|한눈에 봐도 붙잡아 주길 바라는 액션이다. 이럴 때는 또 기대에 부합해 줘야지.
240|
241|“야, 어디 가!”
242|
243|혁무진이 씩씩거리며 말했다.
244|
245|“됐습니다. 다른 건 다 참아도, 제가 아끼는 수하들까지 무시하는 발언은 참을 수 없습니다!”
246|
247|“헉.”
248|
249|“또 왜요?”
250|
251|“네 주둥이에서 그런 말이 나올 줄은 몰랐어서. 무진이 다 컸네. 넌 입에 포경 수술 안 받아도 되겠다.”
252|
253|“……저 진짜 갑니다.”
254|
255|“알았어, 알았어. 앉아. 진정하고 여기 물 한잔해.”
256|
257|“흥. 싫습니다.”
258|
259|“허허. 우리 무진이 진짜 많이 컸네. 두 번 말하게 만들고.”
260|
261|“……!”
262|
263|멈칫한 혁무진이 슬그머니 의자에 엉덩이를 걸쳤다.
264|
265|“그래도 사과는 받아야겠습니다.”
266|
267|“응? 무슨 사과?”
268|
269|“제 수하들 무시하셨던 거요.”
270|
271|“내가 왜? 난 걔들 무시한 적 없어.”
272|
273|“조금 전에는 못 믿으시겠다면서요. 지금 조장님보다 무공 약하다고 무시하신 것 아닙니까?”
274|
275|나는 차갑게 식은 차를 호로록 들이켰다.
276|
277|“뭐, 우리가 구파일방이나 오대세가도 아닌데 그 동네랑 수준 차이는 당연히 나지. 그런데 진룡대 애들, 하나같이 젊고 재능도 뛰어나다며? 어제는 뛰어난 활약도 보였고. 무명을 구한 것도 진룡대 아냐?”
278|
279|소림사는 거목이다. 어제 사건으로 법왕이라는 큰 가지와 수많은 열매를 떨궈야 했지만 뿌리는 남아 있었다.
280|
281|소림의 무공. 그리고 살아남은 무명의 존재가 그것이었다.
282|
283|아, 굉천이라는 노승도 살았다고 했었나?
284|
285|“맞습니다. 암천 놈들과도 물러섬 없이 싸웠고요.”
286|
287|혁무진이 자부심에 가득 찬 얼굴로 가슴을 쭉 폈다.
288|
289|“그래. 그럼 된 거지. 보니까 애들도 똘똘해 보이더만. 가문에 대한 충성심도 깊고. 근데 딱 하나가 문제야.”
290|
291|“그게 뭔데요?”
292|
293|“부대주가 너라는 거.”
294|
295|“…….”
296|
297|“수하들은 아래에서 꼿꼿이 서서 근무하는데, 부대주라는 놈이 여기서 노가리를 까?”
298|
299|“그, 그건…….”
300|
301|“수하들 아낀다며? 자랑스럽다며?”
302|
303|“사실입니다! 제가 얼마나 저 녀석들을 아끼는데…….”
304|
305|주춤했던 혁무진이 정신을 차리고는 기다렸다는 듯 말을 술술 쏟아 냈다.
306|
307|“그리고 제가 이번에 맡은 임무는 적 대협과 조장님의 곁을 지키는 겁니다.”
308|
309|“그전에는?”
310|
311|“예?”
312|
313|“그전에 맡은 임무는 뭐였냐고.”
314|
315|“그거야 당연히 소가주님 경호죠.”
316|
317|“그래?”
318|
319|나는 허허 웃으며 품에서 ‘그것’을 꺼내 탁자 위로 던졌다.
320|

“That’s the problem. No one knows.”

[P86]
“Didn’t some famous physician come by?”

[P87]
“He said there was nothing he could do. Since Old Master wasn’t gravely wounded like the others, he told us to wait and see.”

[P88]
The Dance of the Fire God and Demon. The supreme technique of the Fire Gate Clan.

[P89]
It possessed enough power to contend with a thousand martial artists, but everything came at a price.

[P90]
A man well over a hundred years old simply didn’t have the stamina or strength left to withstand the aftermath.

[P91]
*Maybe…*

[P92]
I shook my head, driving away the thought that had suddenly surfaced.

[P93]
There was no point dwelling on the worst.

[P94]
Both the Sword Saint and the physician had said his life wasn’t in danger. For now, the best thing I could do was stay by Jeok Cheongang’s side and watch over him.

[P95]
“There weren’t any suspicious people around while I was gone, were there?”

[P96]
The Abbot of Shaolin had been assassinated inside the Murim Alliance. No one was safe. Just as Jeok Cheongang had protected me from the Blood Lord, I had to protect him.

[P97]
Hyuk Mujin nodded confidently.

[P98]
“The Jin Dragon Squad has the pavilion completely surrounded. No one can slip through. Don’t worry.”

[P99]
“The Jin Dragon Squad? The elite force of the Taiyuan Jin Family?”

[P100]
“Yes. The Lesser Family Head was concerned for Great Hero Jeok’s safety, so he assigned me here. Who do you think I am? I’m Hyuk Mujin, Vice Squad Leader of the Jin Dragon Squad.”

[P101]
“Uh…”

[P102]
I looked him up and down, then quietly averted my eyes.

[P103]
Hyuk Mujin’s confident expression instantly turned sour.

[P104]
“What was that reaction?”

[P105]
“Nothing. I just realized I shouldn’t leave again.”

[P106]
“Don’t tell me you doubt the Jin Dragon Squad, the finest force in our family?”

[P107]
“Come on. I said that’s not it. Let it go.”

[P108]
Hyuk Mujin glared at me through narrowed eyes, then shot to his feet.

[P109]
“Fine. I’ll report to the Lesser Family Head and have everyone withdrawn.”

[P110]
“Hey, why are you taking it that way? Are you going through puberty or something?”

[P111]
“Because you keep saying such hurtful things, Captain! Is this the first time you’ve done this? Huh?”

[P112]
“Keep your voice down. You’ll wake Old Master.”

[P113]
“It would be nice if he woke up.”

[P114]
“…”

[P115]
He had a point.

[P116]
As I found myself momentarily at a loss for words, Hyuk Mujin headed for the door.

[P117]
One glance told me he was putting on an act because he wanted me to stop him. At times like this, I had to give him what he wanted.

[P118]
“Hey, where are you going?”

[P119]
Hyuk Mujin huffed, “Forget it. I can put up with anything else, but I won’t tolerate you insulting the subordinates I care about!”

[P120]
“Gasp.”

[P121]
“What now?”

[P122]
“I never thought I’d hear words like that come out of your mouth. Mujin, you’ve really grown up. Guess your mouth doesn’t need circumcising after all.”

[P123]
“…I’m really leaving.”

[P124]
“Fine, fine. Sit down. Calm yourself and have some water.”

[P125]
“Hmph. No.”

[P126]
“Well, well. Our Mujin really has grown up. Making me say it twice now.”

[P127]
“…!”

[P128]
Hyuk Mujin froze, then quietly lowered himself onto the chair.

[P129]
“I still deserve an apology.”

[P130]
“Huh? For what?”

[P131]
“For insulting my subordinates.”

[P132]
“Why should I apologize? I never insulted them.”

[P133]
“You just said you didn’t trust them. Isn’t it because they’re weaker in martial arts than you?”

[P134]
I sipped my cold tea.

[P135]
“Well, we’re not the Nine Sects and One Gang or one of the Five Great Families, so of course there’s a difference in strength. But you said every member of the Jin Dragon Squad is young and talented, didn’t you? They distinguished themselves yesterday too. Weren’t they the ones who saved Unnamed?”

[P136]
Shaolin was a mighty tree. Yesterday’s tragedy had cost it a great branch called the Dharma King and countless fruits, but its roots remained.

[P137]
Shaolin’s martial arts. And Unnamed, who had survived.

[P138]
Those were its roots.

[P139]
Oh, and hadn’t they said that old monk Hongcheon survived too?

[P140]
“That’s right. They fought Dark Heaven without giving an inch.”

[P141]
Hyuk Mujin puffed out his chest, his face filled with pride.

[P142]
“Exactly. Then what’s the problem? The kids looked sharp to me. They’re fiercely loyal to the family too. There’s only one problem.”

[P143]
“What’s that?”

[P144]
“You’re their Vice Squad Leader.”

[P145]
“…”

[P146]
“Your subordinates are standing at attention down there, while their Vice Squad Leader sits up here shooting the breeze?”

[P147]
“Th-That’s…”

[P148]
“You said you cared about them. That you were proud of them.”

[P149]
“It’s true! Do you have any idea how much I care about those guys…?”

[P150]
Hyuk Mujin faltered for a moment, then quickly recovered and poured out the words as though he had been waiting for the chance.

[P151]
“Besides, my current mission is to guard Great Hero Jeok and you, Captain.”

[P152]
“And before that?”

[P153]
“Pardon?”

[P154]
“What was your previous mission?”

[P155]
“Guarding the Lesser Family Head, obviously.”

[P156]
“Really?”

[P157]
I chuckled, pulled *that* from inside my robes, and tossed it onto the table.

[P158]
*Clatter.*

[P159]
Hyuk Mujin sucked in a breath at the sight of the golden mask gleaming on the table.

[P160]
“Gasp! W-Where did you get that…?”

[P161]
“Where do you think? I knew this wasn’t like you. No wonder you clung to me so desperately after the preliminaries.”

[P162]
“Wait. You’ve got it all wrong. I was genuinely so busy with guard duty that I barely had time to open my eyes—”

[P163]
“You’ve been misunderstood? Fine. Want me to make sure you never open them again?”

[P164]
*Crack!*

[P165]
The golden mask crumpled into a little ball in my hand. Hyuk Mujin’s eyes shook as though caught in an earthquake.

[P166]
“You were guarding him at a gambling house, you bastard? You’d become so famous I didn’t even have to ask around. Some lunatic won a hundred thousand silver nyang in one shot, then immediately lost all hundred thousand. People were treating him like a legend—not just a legend, but legend-tier.”

[P167]
If the story had reached my ears even in the middle of this crisis, that said everything.

[P168]
I’d even heard a rumor that one of the servants working at the Murim Alliance had hit the jackpot on Toto—no, Dodo—slapped the Chief Steward across the face, and walked out.

[P169]
“If you cared so much about your subordinates, you should’ve collected dues from them and placed the bet together. Did you really hog it all for yourself because you were afraid they’d drive down the odds?”

[P170]
“…”

[P171]
No answer. Nothing to say.

[P172]
Even if he had ten mouths, none of them could have produced an excuse. Hyuk Mujin stood frozen and pale before finally forcing out a few words.

[P173]
“Life is… all about one big score.”

[P174]
“…”

[P175]
This bastard still hadn’t come to his senses.

[P176]
I stared at Hyuk Mujin in disbelief and raised my fist.

[P177]
That was when—

[P178]
*Swish. Tap.*

[P179]
There had been no noticeable presence. No sound.

[P180]
As if by magic, a young man—or rather, an old man—had ascended more than ten jang and landed on the windowsill. He grinned and waved.

[P181]
“Want to talk for a moment, friend?”

[P182]
*Friend, my ass.*

[P183]
I looked at Sword Saint Mae Jonghak and heaved an inward sigh.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;

Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

[P39]
After raining blows down on the back of his head, I finally felt a little better.

[P40]
I already had enough on my mind. Why did this bastard have to rile me up on top of everything else?

[P41]
“Things are serious right now, so watch your mouth. Got it?”

[P42]

[P43]
“Just keep quiet.”

[P44]
“…Yes, sir.”

[P46]
Martial artists hurried frantically in every direction. Though none of them openly showed it, tension hung thick in the air.

[P47]

[P48]
Hyuk Mujin’s subdued voice reached my ears.

[P49]
“It feels strange.”

[P50]
“What does?”

[P51]

[P52]
“I feel the same way.”

[P53]

[P54]
Hong Dao breathing his last. Shaolin Temple drenched in blood. The Yin-Yang Twin Freaks, the Blood Lord, and finally Sword Saint Mae Jonghak.

[P55]
The scenes passed before my eyes like a panorama.

[P56]
*The problem is, that was only the prologue.*

[P57]

[P58]

[P59]
*Something is changing.*

[P60]
The world had already become a massive powder keg. The orthodox faction held the fuse, but Dark Heaven had the flint.

[P61]

[P62]
I didn’t know how all this would end, but I could guess what would happen along the way.

[P63]
*There’s going to be a war.*

[P64]
A war on an entirely different scale from the one in Shanxi Province.

[P65]
There was no way the people at the top had failed to realize what even I suspected.

[P66]
The leaders of the orthodox faction were already consumed with handling the aftermath and holding meetings about the incident.

[P67]
“Come to think of it, Captain, didn’t you attend yesterday’s meeting too?”

[P68]
I nodded slightly.

[P69]
The Jin Family of Taiyuan might not compare to the Nine Sects and One Gang or the Five Great Families, but it was still the undisputed hegemon of Shanxi Province.

[P70]
And since Shanxi Province was where Dark Heaven had first revealed itself, it was only natural for the leaders to take a keen interest in us.

[P71]
“What did they say?”

[P72]
“They asked about the Head Elder and the Red Wind Band. I told them everything I knew.”

[P73]
“The Head Elder is one thing, but why the Red Wind Band?”

[P74]
“The Temporary Strength Pill used by Pung Yang, the Red Wind Band Leader, is connected to Dark Heaven.”

[P75]
“Ah.”

[P76]
Hyuk Mujin was now a high-ranking member of the family, so he had some idea of what was going on. He knew about both the Temporary Strength Pill and Dark Heaven.

[P77]
“Did they say anything else?”

[P78]
“No. I just left. My eldest brother will hear any important news and pass it on anyway…”

[P79]
My voice sank without me realizing it.

[P80]
“I didn’t feel comfortable leaving Old Master alone for too long.”

[P81]
My gaze drifted from the window toward a lone figure.

[P82]
A small elderly man lay on the bed as though deeply asleep.

[P83]
When I took his wrinkled hand, I could feel his pulse. The faint rise and fall of his chest told me he was breathing. But even after a full day, he still hadn’t regained consciousness.

[P84]
“When do you think he’ll wake up?”

[P85]
“That’s the problem. No one knows.”

[P86]
“Didn’t some famous physician come by?”

[P87]
“He said there was nothing he could do. Since Old Master wasn’t gravely wounded like the others, he told us to wait and see.”

[P88]
The Dance of the Fire God and Demon. The supreme technique of the Fire Gate Clan.

[P89]
It possessed enough power to contend with a thousand martial artists, but everything came at a price.

[P90]
A man well over a hundred years old simply didn’t have the stamina or strength left to withstand the aftermath.

[P91]
*Maybe…*

[P92]
I shook my head, driving away the thought that had suddenly surfaced.

[P93]
There was no point dwelling on the worst.

[P94]
Both the Sword Saint and the physician had said his life wasn’t in danger. For now, the best thing I could do was stay by Jeok Cheongang’s side and watch over him.

[P95]
“There weren’t any suspicious people around while I was gone, were there?”

[P96]
The Abbot of Shaolin had been assassinated inside the Murim Alliance. No one was safe. Just as Jeok Cheongang had protected me from the Blood Lord, I had to protect him.

[P97]
Hyuk Mujin nodded confidently.

[P98]
“The Jin Dragon Squad has the pavilion completely surrounded. No one can slip through. Don’t worry.”

[P99]
“The Jin Dragon Squad? The elite force of the Taiyuan Jin Family?”

[P100]
“Yes. The Lesser Family Head was concerned for Great Hero Jeok’s safety, so he assigned me here. Who do you think I am? I’m Hyuk Mujin, Vice Squad Leader of the Jin Dragon Squad.”

[P101]
“Uh…”

[P102]
I looked him up and down, then quietly averted my eyes.

[P103]
Hyuk Mujin’s confident expression instantly turned sour.

[P104]
“What was that reaction?”

[P105]
“Nothing. I just realized I shouldn’t leave again.”

[P106]
“Don’t tell me you doubt the Jin Dragon Squad, the finest force in our family?”

[P107]
“Come on. I said that’s not it. Let it go.”

[P108]
Hyuk Mujin glared at me through narrowed eyes, then shot to his feet.

[P109]
“Fine. I’ll report to the Lesser Family Head and have everyone withdrawn.”

[P110]
“Hey, why are you taking it that way? Are you going through puberty or something?”

[P111]
“Because you keep saying such hurtful things, Captain! Is this the first time you’ve done this? Huh?”

[P112]
“Keep your voice down. You’ll wake Old Master.”

[P113]
“It would be nice if he woke up.”

[P114]
“…”

[P115]
He had a point.

[P116]
As I found myself momentarily at a loss for words, Hyuk Mujin headed for the door.

[P117]
One glance told me he was putting on an act because he wanted me to stop him. At times like this, I had to give him what he wanted.

[P118]
“Hey, where are you going?”

[P119]
Hyuk Mujin huffed, “Forget it. I can put up with anything else, but I won’t tolerate you insulting the subordinates I care about!”

[P120]
“Gasp.”

[P121]
“What now?”

[P122]
“I never thought I’d hear words like that come out of your mouth. Mujin, you’ve really grown up. Guess your mouth doesn’t need circumcising after all.”

[P123]
“…I’m really leaving.”

[P124]
“Fine, fine. Sit down. Calm yourself and have some water.”

[P125]
“Hmph. No.”

[P126]
“Well, well. Our Mujin really has grown up. Making me say it twice now.”

[P127]
“…!”

[P128]
Hyuk Mujin froze, then quietly lowered himself onto the chair.

[P129]
“I still deserve an apology.”

[P130]
“Huh? For what?”

[P131]
“For insulting my subordinates.”

[P132]
“Why should I apologize? I never insulted them.”

[P133]
“You just said you didn’t trust them. Isn’t it because they’re weaker in martial arts than you?”

[P134]
I sipped my cold tea.

[P135]
“Well, we’re not the Nine Sects and One Gang or one of the Five Great Families, so of course there’s a difference in strength. But you said every member of the Jin Dragon Squad is young and talented, didn’t you? They distinguished themselves yesterday too. Weren’t they the ones who saved Unnamed?”

[P136]
Shaolin was a mighty tree. Yesterday’s tragedy had cost it a great branch called the Dharma King and countless fruits, but its roots remained.

[P137]
Shaolin’s martial arts. And Unnamed, who had survived.

[P138]
Those were its roots.

[P139]
Oh, and hadn’t they said that old monk Hongcheon survived too?

[P140]
“That’s right. They fought Dark Heaven without giving an inch.”

[P141]
Hyuk Mujin puffed out his chest, his face filled with pride.

[P142]
“Exactly. Then what’s the problem? The kids looked sharp to me. They’re fiercely loyal to the family too. There’s only one problem.”

[P143]
“What’s that?”

[P144]
“You’re their Vice Squad Leader.”

[P145]
“…”

[P146]
“Your subordinates are standing at attention down there, while their Vice Squad Leader sits up here shooting the breeze?”

[P147]
“Th-That’s…”

[P148]
“You said you cared about them. That you were proud of them.”

[P149]
“It’s true! Do you have any idea how much I care about those guys…?”

[P150]
Hyuk Mujin faltered for a moment, then quickly recovered and poured out the words as though he had been waiting for the chance.

[P151]
“Besides, my current mission is to guard Great Hero Jeok and you, Captain.”

[P152]
“And before that?”

[P153]
“Pardon?”

[P154]
“What was your previous mission?”

[P155]
“Guarding the Lesser Family Head, obviously.”

[P156]
“Really?”

[P157]
I chuckled, pulled *that* from inside my robes, and tossed it onto the table.

[P158]
*Clatter.*

[P159]
Hyuk Mujin sucked in a breath at the sight of the golden mask gleaming on the table.

[P160]
“Gasp! W-Where did you get that…?”

[P161]
“Where do you think? I knew this wasn’t like you. No wonder you clung to me so desperately after the preliminaries.”

[P162]
“Wait. You’ve got it all wrong. I was genuinely so busy with guard duty that I barely had time to open my eyes—”

[P163]
“You’ve been misunderstood? Fine. Want me to make sure you never open them again?”

[P164]
*Crack!*

[P165]
The golden mask crumpled into a little ball in my hand. Hyuk Mujin’s eyes shook as though caught in an earthquake.

[P166]
“You were guarding him at a gambling house, you bastard? You’d become so famous I didn’t even have to ask around. Some lunatic won a hundred thousand silver nyang in one shot, then immediately lost all hundred thousand. People were treating him like a legend—not just a legend, but legend-tier.”

[P167]
If the story had reached my ears even in the middle of this crisis, that said everything.

[P168]
I’d even heard a rumor that one of the servants working at the Murim Alliance had hit the jackpot on Toto—no, Dodo—slapped the Chief Steward across the face, and walked out.

[P169]
“If you cared so much about your subordinates, you should’ve collected dues from them and placed the bet together. Did you really hog it all for yourself because you were afraid they’d drive down the odds?”

[P170]
“…”

[P171]
No answer. Nothing to say.

[P172]
Even if he had ten mouths, none of them could have produced an excuse. Hyuk Mujin stood frozen and pale before finally forcing out a few words.

[P173]
“Life is… all about one big score.”

[P174]
“…”

[P175]
This bastard still hadn’t come to his senses.

[P176]
I stared at Hyuk Mujin in disbelief and raised my fist.

[P177]
That was when—

[P178]
*Swish. Tap.*

[P179]
There had been no noticeable presence. No sound.

[P180]
As if by magic, a young man—or rather, an old man—had ascended more than ten jang and landed on the windowsill. He grinned and waved.

[P181]
“Want to talk for a moment, friend?”

[P182]
*Friend, my ass.*

[P183]
I looked at Sword Saint Mae Jonghak and heaved an inward sigh.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 268

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃268화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|법왕 굉도의 죽음. 그리고 무림의 태산북두인 소림사에서 벌어진 의문의 혈겁(血劫).
  6|
  7|달리는 말보다 빠른 것이 사람들의 목소리다.
  8|
  9|수많은 목격자들의 입을 통해 소문은 일파만파 퍼졌다.
 10|
 11|“다들 그 소식 들었나? 성라대연에서…….”
 12|
 13|“무림인들이 숭산을 에워싸고 있네. 소림사에서 혈겁이 벌어졌다더군.”
 14|
 15|성라대연을 맞이하여 축제 분위기에 들떠 있던 하남성은 발칵 뒤집혔다.
 16|
 17|노인은 수십여 년 전 천하를 휩쓸었던 마교의 준동을 떠올렸고, 젊은이는 케케묵은 과거라 취급했던 전쟁이 현실로 다가왔다는 사실을 깨달았다.
 18|
 19|“마교가 나타나다니, 큰일이야. 큰일.”
 20|
 21|“일설에 의하면 마교가 아니라 다른 놈들이 저지른 짓이라던데?”
 22|
 23|“그런 짓을 저지를 만한 놈들이 마교 말고도 또 있단 말인가?”
 24|
 25|“정확한 사실까지는 나도 잘 몰라. 그냥 오다가다 들었네.”
 26|
 27|“그럴 리가. 이번에 소림을 습격한 흉수들의 우두머리가 그 무시무시한 음양쌍괴(陰陽雙怪)라던데.”
 28|
 29|“음양쌍괴? 나는 마교주인 천마(天魔)가 직접 나섰다고 들었네만.”
 30|
 31|“처, 천마?”
 32|
 33|여러 가지 말들이 쌓이고 쌓이니 소문은 눈덩이처럼 불어났다.
 34|
 35|사실과 거짓 속에서 혼란을 겪던 사람들의 이목이 한 곳을 향해 쏠린 것은 당연한 일이었다.
 36|
 37|무림맹의 옛터.
 38|
 39|정파 무림의 크고 작은 기둥들이 위치한 그곳으로.
 40|
 41|
 42|
 43|* * *
 44|
 45|
 46|
 47|“이야기 들었습니다. 종리추, 아니 검성 매종학 대협에 관해서요.”
 48|
 49|“…….”
 50|
 51|“힘내십쇼. 살다 보면 그럴 수도 있죠.”
 52|
 53|“…….”
 54|
 55|“저도 이번에 완전히 알거지, 휴우……. 여하간 그렇게 됐는데. 조장님 소식 듣고 힘이 솟더라고요.”
 56|
 57|“왜?”
 58|
 59|“예?”
 60|
 61|“왜 힘이 솟냐고.”
 62|
 63|“그거야 당연한 이치 아닙니까. 옛 성현들이 말씀하시길, 아픔은 나눌수록 가벼워진다고…….”
 64|
 65|퍽!
 66|
 67|“흐억.”
 68|
 69|정확히 명치를 가격당한 혁무진이 바람 빠지는 소리를 내며 허리를 숙였다.
 70|
 71|훤히 드러난 뒤통수를 보자 저절로 손이 간다. 손이 가.
 72|
 73|빡!
 74|
 75|“힘이 솟구치냐? 어?”
 76|
 77|“자, 잠시만요. 명치 맞았어요. 명치.”
 78|
 79|“저는요. 니 새끼 때문에 혈압이 솟구쳐요. 피가 거꾸로 솟아요!”
 80|
 81|빡빡빡!
 82|
 83|폭풍처럼 뒤통수를 후려치고 나자 속이 좀 풀린다.
 84|
 85|이 자식은 가뜩이나 심란한데 사람을 건드리고 난리야.
 86|
 87|“지금 분위기 심각하니까 말조심해라. 응?”
 88|
 89|혁무진이 뒤통수를 문지르며 중얼거렸다.
 90|
 91|“너무 심각해 보여서 풀어 드리려고 한 건데.”
 92|
 93|“그냥 조용히 있어, 인마.”
 94|
 95|“……옙.”
 96|
 97|혁무진을 침묵시킨 나는 가만히 창밖을 바라봤다.
 98|
 99|정신없이 사방을 오고 가는 무인들과 누구 하나 티 내는 사람이 없는데도 긴장감이 흐르는 분위기.
100|
101|그러나 그 와중에도 하늘은 화창하기 그지없었다.
102|
103|힘 빠진 혁무진의 목소리가 귓가를 파고들었다.
104|
105|“기분이 이상하네요.”
106|
107|“뭐가.”
108|
109|“그냥. 다 실감이 안 나요. 고작 하루밖에 지나지 않았다는 것이.”
110|
111|“나도 그래.”
112|
113|파란만장이라는 말로도 부족하다. 전날 있었던 모든 일이 무엇 하나 실감 나지 않았다. 전부 꿈처럼 느껴질 만큼.
114|
115|마지막 숨을 내쉬던 굉도와 피로 물든 소림사의 광경이 눈앞을 스치고 음양쌍괴와 혈주, 검성 매종학의 등장까지 파노라마처럼 펼쳐졌다.
116|
117|‘문제는 이게 프롤로그라는 거지.’
118|
119|영화관이었다면 슬슬 엔딩 크레딧이 올라와도 이상하지 않은 타이밍. 하지만 이건 불길한 전조에 지나지 않는다.
120|
121|모두가 예감하는 왠지 모를 위기감이 피부로 느껴질 정도였다.
122|
123|‘뭔가가 바뀌고 있다.’
124|
125|작금의 천하는 이미 거대한 화약고로 변해 버렸다. 도화선을 쥔 것은 정파 무림이지만 암천의 손에는 부싯돌이 들려 있었다.
126|
127|그리고 바로 어제, 도화선에 불이 붙었다.
128|
129|이 모든 일의 결말은 아직 모르겠지만 과정은 짐작할 수 있었다.
130|
131|‘전쟁이 일어나겠지.’
132|
133|산서성 때와는 차원이 다른 전쟁이 일어날 것이다.
134|
135|나도 내심 짐작하고 있는 것을 수뇌부가 모를 리 없다.
136|
137|정파 무림의 수뇌부는 이미 이번 사건의 사태 수습과 회의에 여념이 없었다.
138|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
